title: Ben Thanh Market
text: Ben Thanh Market, one of Ho Chi Minh City's busiest markets, is not just a shopping destination but also a food paradise and a cultural icon. Visitors can explore countless stalls offering various goods, from fresh produce to clothing. Ben Thanh Market is known as a traditional market and an indispensable part of the history and culture of Ho Chi Minh City. With its unique architecture and central location, the Ben Thanh Market attracts millions of tourists every year. Visiting Ben Thanh market is a famous thing to do in Ho Chi Minh city. Ben Thanh Market is located on Le Loi Street, Ben Thanh Ward, District 1. This location can be considered the 'heart' of the city, very convenient for travel and sightseeing. The market is only about 500m from the City Opera House, another famous landmark of Saigon. Around the market, there are many shops, restaurants, and cafes, meeting visitors' shopping and dining needs. In front of the market is Ben Thanh roundabout, an important traffic point and a city symbol. The Ben Thanh Market has 4 main entrances located on major streets such as Phan Chu Trinh, Phan Boi Chau, Le Thanh Ton, and the square of Quach Thi Trang. With its central location and outstanding features, the market is not only a shopping destination but also a gateway connecting visitors to rich tourist attractions and services, helping them fully experience the vibrant life and local culture of Saigon. The day market opens from 6:00 - 18:00 and the night market opens from 18:00 -22:00.

title: Notre Dame Cathedral
text: Notre Dame Cathedral in Vietnam is honored as one of the world's 19 most majestic cathedrals, the only representative from Southeast Asia. This long-lasting masterpiece, seen as the architectural symbol of Ho Chi Minh City, hosts a flock of new tourists every day who seek ancient grandeur, holiness, and enchanting photography spots. Besides having the vibrancy of a financial hub, Ho Chi Minh City (aka Saigon) retains historical vestiges captivating both domestic and international tourists. Standing out in the heart of the city, Notre Dame Cathedral in Vietnam is not only a sought-after attraction in Saigon but also the most emblematic landmark in the country, let alone the city. This article will provide you with the essential information you need to know for your visit to this famous religious site. The cathedral is located at No.1 Cong xa Paris St, Sai Gon Ward, Ho Chi Minh City. Opening hours for Notre-Dame Cathedral Basilica of Saigon: 5:00-6:15 and 16:45-18:30 on Mondays and Tuesdays; 5:00-6:15 on Wednesdays; 5:00-6:15 and 16:45-21:00 on Thursdays and Fridays; 5:00-6:15 and 16:45-19:00 on Saturdays; and 5:00-11:00 and 15:30-20:30 on Sundays. Weekday Masses are held at 5:30 and 17:30. Sunday Masses are held at 5:30, 6:45, 8:00, 9:30 (English-language Mass), 16:00, 17:30, and 18:30.

title: Independence Palace
text: The Independence Palace (Vietnamese: Dinh Độc Lập), also publicly and officially known as the Reunification Convention Hall or simply Reunification Hall (Vietnamese: Hội trường Thống Nhất), is a historic landmark and government-owned public hall in Ho Chi Minh City (formerly known as Saigon), Vietnam. It was designed by architect Ngô Viết Thụ and was the presidential palace, home and workplace of the president of the Republic of Vietnam (South Vietnam). It was also the site of the Fall of Saigon on 30 April 1975 that ended the Vietnam War, when a Liberation Army of South Vietnam tank crashed through its gates. After the reunification of Vietnam, the building continued to serve as a government and presidential office until 1976 when the capital of South Vietnam was officially moved to Hanoi, and the government's functions were relocated. The palace is now preserved as a convention hall for state events, and also as a museum that is open to the public, and is a popular tourist attraction in Ho Chi Minh City. Location: 135 Nam Ky Khoi Nghia Street, Ben Thanh, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. Opening hour: from 7:00 to 18:00 every day

title: The War Remnants Museum
text: The War Remnants Museum, established on September 4, 1975, is a member of the Vietnam Museum System, INMP and ICOM. The museum specializes in researching, collecting, preserving and displaying evidence of crimes and consequences of the war of aggression against Vietnam, thereby calling for awareness against unjust wars, protecting peace and promoting solidarity between nations. With 9 permanent exhibition themes, many short-term, mobile exhibitions and activities to interact with war witnesses, the Museum welcomes nearly 1 million visitors each year and is a cultural - tourism destination that attracts a large number of domestic and foreign public. Ticket counter at the front gate is located at 28 Vo Van Tan Street, Xuan Hoa Ward, Ho Chi Minh City and the ticket counter at the back gate is located at Le Quy Don Street, Xuan Hoa Ward, Ho Chi Minh City. Opening hour: The museum welcomes visitors from 7:30 to 17:30 every day including holidays but the ticket counter at Vo Van Tan gate only opens from 7:30 to 17:00 daily

title: Nguyen Hue Walking Street
text: Nguyen Hue Walking Street is the cultural hub of Ho Chi Minh City. Home to unique culinary delights, lively bars and exciting entertainment venues, it is the perfect destination for nightlife lovers. Nguyen Hue Walking Street is located in the heart of Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. This bustling, lively street is conveniently situated near many of the city’s most famous attractions and destinations. The street is a hub of excitement and energy, offering a diverse range of bars, clubs, and entertainment options that cater to every taste and budget. Thanks to its diversity, Nguyen Hue Pedestrian Street is a popular destination for tourists and locals alike. From sophisticated bars to bustling street markets, everyone can find something to enjoy on Nguyen Hue Street. What sets Nguyen Hue Street apart from other nightlife destinations is its unique atmosphere. This street is alive with the sound of music and laughter, and the air is always filled with excitement. Location: District 1, downtown Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. Opening hours: Open 24/7, but most activities happen from 5:00 PM to midnight.

title: Bach Dang Wharf Park
text: Bach Dang Wharf Park, a hidden gem in the heart of Ho Chi Minh City, offers an oasis of tranquility amidst the bustling urban landscape. Nestled along the Saigon River, this park offers visitors breathtaking views, lush greenery, and a serene atmosphere perfect for relaxation and recreation. Situated at the intersection of Ton Duc Thang and Hai Ba Trung streets in District 1, Bach Dang Wharf Park is easily accessible by various means of transportation. The park’s central location makes it a convenient spot for both locals and tourists. Public buses, taxis, and ride-hailing services like Grab, and bikes are readily available, ensuring a hassle-free journey to this picturesque park. Location: No 2, Ton Duc Thang Street, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City. Opening hour: Open 24/7

title: Sai Gon Zoo and Botanical Gardens
text: The Saigon Zoo and Botanical Gardens or locally and colloquially known as The Zoo ('Sở Thú'), is Vietnam's oldest zoo and botanical garden. The Saigon Zoo and Botanical Gardens was commissioned by Admiral Pierre-Paul de La Grandière in 1864, and was opened to the public in 1869, making it one of the world's oldest continuously operating zoos. Located on Nguyen Binh Khiem Street and the northeast end of Le Duan Boulevard in District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, it is home to over a hundred species of mammals, reptiles and birds, as well as many rare orchids and ornamental plants. Also within the grounds is the Ho Chi Minh City Museum of History, housing some 25,000 artifacts of history, culture and ethnography of South Vietnam. The grounds also include the Temple of Hùng King (formerly a monument to Indochinese soldiers who died for France during World War I). Other parts of the zoo are divided into animal and plant conservation areas, an orchid garden, and an amusement park. The Saigon Zoo and Botanical Garden contains 590 animals of 125 species and 1,830 trees and plants of 260 species, some of which are over 100 years old. This includes 20 species of orchid, 32 species of cactus and 34 species of bonsai. The Saigon Zoo and Botanical Garden is divided into an animal conservation area, a plant conservation area, an orchid garden and an amusement park. Location: 2B Nguyen Binh Khiem Street (Main Gate) or No.1 Nguyen Thi Minh Khai Street, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City. Opening hour: 7:00 to 18:00 every day

title: Tan Dinh Parish Church
text: Tan Dinh Church or Tan Dinh Parish Church is a Roman Catholic church in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. Its formal name is the Church of the Sacred Heart of Jesus. Even though it is in District 3, the parish shares its name with neighbouring District 1's Tan Dinh ward as of Tan Dinh was the place name of a former village that the church was also included. It was built during the French colonial period in the 1870s and completed on 16 December 1876, when Vietnam was part of French Indochina. The architecture is mainly neo-Romanesque, but it also has some neo-Gothic and neo-Renaissance elements. It has been painted pastel-pink both on the exterior and interior since 1957, earning it the nickname 'the pink church'.It is the second-largest church in Ho Chi Minh City, after Notre-Dame Basilica in District 1.[citation needed] They both belong to the Archdiocese of Ho Chi Minh City but different deanery when Tan Dinh Church is belong to the same name deanery while the Notre-Dame Basilica is Sai Gon - Cho Quan. Tan Dinh Church is not a cathedral; Notre-Dame is the cathedral (seat) of this metropolitan archdiocese. Location: Xuan Hoa, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City. Opening hour: everyday from 7:00 to 12:00 pm on the morning, from 14:00 to 17:00 on the afternoon, from 20:00 to 21:00 on the evening

title: Landmark 81
text: Landmark 81 is a supertall skyscraper in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. It is primarily invested in and developed by Vinhomes, the largest Vietnamese real-estate developer. Landmark 81 holds the position of the tallest building in Vietnam, the second-tallest building in Southeast Asia, as well as the seventeenth-tallest building in the world overall. The 461.2-metre-tall (1,513 ft), 81-story building is located where the Newport logistics base was on the western banks of the Saigon River in Thanh My Tay ward, located in the northeast side of Ho Chi Minh City's historic center and to the immediate southern side of Saigon Bridge. The tower is built at the heart of Vinhomes Central Park, a $1.5 billion high-end mixed-use urban development. The development comprises an Autograph Collection hotel (developed by Vinpearl and originally known as Vinpearl Landmark 81 Hotel) with conference facilities, luxury apartments, the Vincom Center Landmark 81 Mall (the second high-end retail spaces of Vingroup in Ho Chi Minh City after the Vincom Center Dong Khoi), officetel, restaurants, bars, and a multi-story observation deck. Location: Vinhomes Central Park (Saigon Newport), 720A Dien Bien Phu Street, Thanh My Tay, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. Opening hour: the Vincom Center Landmark 81 shopping mall is open from 10:00 AM to 10:00 PM on Monday through Friday, and from 9:30 AM to 10:00 PM on Saturdays and Sundays, opening hours for the different areas inside and around Landmark 81 vary

title: Nguyen Van Binh Book Street
text: Ho Chi Minh City Book Street (also known as Nguyen Van Binh Book Street) is a peaceful retreat nestled in the heart of the bustling city, perfect for book lovers and cultural enthusiasts alike. Lined with charming bookstores, cozy cafés, and lively literary events, this hidden gem offers a unique escape from the fast-paced rhythm of Saigon. Ho Chi Minh City Book Street is located at Nguyen Van Binh Street, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City. Officially known as Nguyen Van Binh Book Street, this pedestrian-only cultural hub is nestled right next to two of Ho Chi Minh City’s most iconic landmarks: Notre-Dame Cathedral and the Central Post Office – architectural gems with a strong French colonial influence. Flanked by tall, leafy trees and dotted with cute cafés and cozy book shops, the entire street feels like a peaceful escape. Here, you can sip on an iced coffee while flipping through a good read, all under dappled sunlight and birdsong. Opening hour: 8:00 - 21:00 from Monday to Friday, 8:00 - 21:30 from Saturday to Sunday.

title: Cu Chi tunnels
text: The tunnels of Cu Chi, are an immense network of connecting tunnels located in the Cu Chi District of Ho Chi Minh City (Saigon), Vietnam, and are part of a much larger network of tunnels that underlie much of the country. The Cu Chi tunnels were the location of several military campaigns during the Vietnam War, and were the Viet Cong's base of operations for the Tet Offensive in 1968. The tunnels were used by Viet Cong soldiers as hiding spots during combat, as well as serving as communication and supply routes, hospitals, food and weapon caches and living quarters for numerous North Vietnamese fighters. The tunnel systems were of great importance to the Viet Cong in their resistance to American and ARVN forces, and helped to counter the growing American military presence. The tunnels contained various bamboo traps made by the Viet Cong to injure and potentially kill American Tunnel Rats if they breached the tunnels. The tunnels also contained ventilation shafts to release smoke from fire and any poisonous gases pumped into the tunnels by the American troops. Location: Provincial Road 15, Phu Hiep Hamlet, Phu My Hung Commune, Cu Chi District, Ho Chi Minh City. Opening hour: 7:00 - 17:00 every day

title: Saigon Central Post Office
text: Located in Cong Xa Paris, Ben Nghe, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Saigon Central Post Office is one of Southeast Asia’s oldest functioning post offices and a rare example of colonial-era architecture still in operation. More than a historic landmark, it preserves Vietnam’s postal and communication heritage. A visit offers a glimpse into the past while still allowing visitors to send postcards, bridging history with the present. Saigon Central Post Office captivates visitors with its distinctive architectural charm, where elegant French design meets Vietnamese cultural influences. From its grand façade to intricate interior details, every element tells a story of history and artistry. The Saigon Post Office is one of Ho Chi Minh City’s most iconic landmarks, standing for over 130 years, embodying the spirit of Saigon’s rich heritage. Built during the French colonial era, it was more than a communication hub, remaining a striking symbol of the city's architectural and historical heritage. Opening hour: 7:30 - 18:00 from Monday to Saturday, 8:00 - 17:00 on Sunday
